sections.html:
Ogden is the Weber County seat, about 40 miles north of Salt Lake City and 10 miles east of the Great Salt Lake. It covers 27.55 square miles and climbs from the valley floor to the Wasatch foothills on its east side. The 2020 census counted 87,321 residents.

The city splits into six districts. The North End holds West Ogden, Downtown and East Central, and the East side includes the East Bench and Shadow Valley. South Ogden, Roy, West Haven, Marriott-Slaterville, Farr West, Harrisville, Pleasant View and North Ogden border it.

About 61.3% of homes are owner-occupied, across 33,508 households. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $355,600, median gross rent is $1,216 and median household income is $72,575.

These are citywide medians. Mean travel time to work is 22.5 minutes.

sections.h2: A rail town with a long history
sections.html:
Ogden began as Fort Buenaventura, built in 1846 by the trapper Miles Goodyear a mile west of today's downtown. Captain James Brown bought it in November 1847 for $3,000, and the city incorporated on February 6, 1851. It later took the name of Peter Skene Ogden.

The city grew up as a rail hub, being the closest large city to Promontory Summit, where the first transcontinental railroad was joined in 1869. Freight still moves through, and FrontRunner commuter rail now carries riders to Salt Lake City and Provo. The National Park Service named Ogden a World War II Heritage City on September 17, 2024.

Ogden's historic districts include Historic 25th Street, Eccles Avenue and Jefferson Avenue. Union Station, Peery's Egyptian Theatre and the Ogden Nature Center are local landmarks.

The city's housing element, amended in 2022, reports that over 44 percent of Ogden's housing was built before 1940, against 27.2 percent in Weber County. That figure comes from an older section of the plan, so treat it as a rough guide. Still, a seller with a house from the early twentieth century should expect questions about wiring, plumbing, the roof and the foundation.

The same plan lists three projects approved as moderate-income housing actions: Lotus Riverwalk Phase 2 with 174 units, Meadowbrook with 48 and Capital Square with 176. It also describes the R-9 zone in the 9 Rails Creative District, which allows up to 29 units per acre, and cottage lots of 1,500 square feet within two blocks of the bus rapid transit route. New construction like this gives buyers more choices, so price your house against what is actually for sale nearby.

sections.h2: Winter, heat and the Wasatch Fault
sections.html:
Summers run hot and fairly dry, with highs often reaching 95 degrees, and winters bring snow from about late October or early November until around April. A roof and heating system that handle both matter to buyers. Average annual precipitation is 16.36 inches.

Ogden also lies along the Wasatch Fault. The Weber segment last produced a major earthquake roughly 200 to 700 years ago, and each active segment can generate a quake as large as about magnitude 7.5. An older house may merit a structural check before listing.

sections.h2: Which school district an address is in
sections.html: Ogden City School District's boundary matches the city limits. Weber School District serves areas outside the city, even when those homes carry an Ogden mailing address. A listing that says Ogden therefore doesn't settle which district a house is in, so confirm it for the address. Buyers with children often ask, and a quick check with the district saves a misunderstanding later.

FrontRunner links Ogden Central Station directly with Salt Lake City. The OGX bus line runs between that station and Weber State University, and other UTA routes reach Brigham City, Weber County and Davis County. Ogden-Hinckley Airport is Utah's busiest municipal airport, and Breeze Airways provides its only commercial service, with nonstop flights to Orange County, California.

Every residential rental in Ogden needs a license, and it is unlawful to occupy a rental without one. Applications are emailed to businesslicense@ogdencity.com. An invoice follows, and payment is required before the license is issued.

Short-term rentals face tighter limits under city code 15-13-38.

  • A sale voids a short-term rental license unless the new owner gets a new one within 90 days and before operating.
  • In R-1 zones only owner-occupied rentals are allowed, and a non-owner-occupied rental in a residential zone needs three years of continuous ownership.
  • Non-owner-occupied units are inspected every two years, and a revoked property is barred from short-term use for three years.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per sleeping room, and parking must be on site.

If the house you are selling has been used as an Airbnb, check your license status before a buyer's agent asks. Because a sale voids the short-term license, tell a buyer who plans to continue the rental that they need to start the new application right away.

Weber County bills Ogden property taxes. Every parcel is valued as of January 1.

Tax stepWhen
Valuation notices mailedAbout July 20
Deadline to appeal valuesSeptember 15 (within 45 days of the notice)
Tax notices mailedMid-October
Deadline to pay without penaltyNovember 30
Delinquent, penalty appliedDecember 1, the greater of 1% or $10
Interest beginsFebruary 1, retroactive to January 1

Appeals go to the Clerk/Auditor at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 320, and the valuation notice comes with an application. Any tax relief shows on the tax notice, not the valuation notice, so check the right document before you assume a break was applied.

Deeds are recorded with the Weber County Recorder, which charges $45 for the first page of a recording and nothing for additional pages, with $2 for each description over ten. Your title company normally pays these at closing and files the deed for you, so you will not usually stand in line at the counter.

sections.h2: Selling an Ogden house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the listing, the buyer's loan and the appraisal. You describe the house, we make an offer based on its condition, and a title company handles signing and recording.

  1. Tell us the address and what shape the house is in.
  2. We review the details, including any rental license or short-term rental permit.
  3. You decide whether to accept our offer.
  4. The title company closes the sale and records the deed.

Ogden sellers often have older houses, rentals or inherited property, and many are not sure what to do first. The first step is just a conversation about the house. If you hold a rental license, bring it along, plus your latest tax notice, so we can go over the details before an offer.

faqs.q: What is the population of Ogden, Utah?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 87,321 people in Ogden.

faqs.q: When are Weber County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the deadline to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, with a penalty of the greater of 1 percent or $10.

faqs.q: Is every Ogden address in Ogden City School District?
faqs.a: No. That district matches the city limits, while Weber School District serves areas outside it even if the address says Ogden.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Ogden?
faqs.a: Yes, all residential rentals need one, and occupying an unlicensed rental is unlawful. For a short-term rental, a new owner has 90 days after a sale to get a new license.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Ogden property valuation?
faqs.a: Send the application that comes with your valuation notice to the Clerk/Auditor at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 320, by September 15.
